title: Ten or more grouped dwellings: at least 20% of dwellings at silver level universal design
text: C2.7.1 Where 10 or more grouped dwellings are proposed, a minimum 20 per cent(1) of all dwellings are: i. designed and constructed to a minimum silver level universal design in accordance with A4 Universal design requirements, or ii. certified Livable Housing Australia to a minimum silver level of performance. Note: No universal design provisions apply for grouped dwellings development with less than 10 dwellings. All other provisions of the R-Codes still apply. (1) Where calculations result in a fraction of a dwelling, the provision is to be rounded up to the nearest whole number.

replaces.note: new for grouped developments of 10+ dwellings at R25 and below (Part B had no universal design requirement)

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: diverges: Chapter 2 C2.7.1 is the gold-level site area variation (its Chapter 3 twin is C2.7.2); this 20% silver clause has no Chapter 2 equivalent. Footnote 1: a fraction of a dwelling rounds up; percentage >= 20 of an integer count is the same test as count >= ceil(0.2 x dwellings). Silver means silver or better. Cross-reference to 'A4' is stale: universal design requirements are Appendix A2 in the draft (register ch3-036).
